data.narrative:
Alsym Energy is a Series C-stage climate and energy company that has raised approximately $110–111M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set spanning one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers across the climate and energy sector, with particular focus on three same-stage private comparables: KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

The peer-median method, applied across the three Series C climate and energy peers, yields a median valuation of $1.0B. The underlying peer range spans $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals), reflecting material heterogeneity within the cohort. This single triangulation method provides the primary quantitative anchor for valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $850M to $1.1B, centered on the $1.0B peer median. This implies a post-money multiple of approximately 7.6–8.8x on deployed capital. Key uncertainties include the limited sample size (one applicable method across three peers) and wide dispersion in the peer set, particularly the $3.0B outlier, which constrains confidence in the range. Additional methodologies—revenue multiples, DCF analysis, or transaction comparables—would be required to meaningfully narrow the range or validate this peer-based estimate. Technology maturity and path to commercialization remain material but unquantified drivers of relative positioning within the range.
